headline: Keep {arm:September}. Both candidates increase cost and degrade character adherence.
lede: Neither challenger improves performance, while {arm:1017} costs {cost.gap.1017.September.multiple} and {arm:qwen3.8-flash} costs {cost.gap.qwen3.8-flash.September.multiple} the control per reply. A switch would require a candidate to demonstrate clear adherence gains or substantial cost reduction.

slots.text: Retain {arm:September}. It delivers the highest adherence at {scoreboard.September.reply_cost_usd|usd_per_1k}, outperforming both candidates on cost and quality.

{arm:1017} regresses adherence by {contrast.1017.persona.holds_character.delta|abs|pts} points while costing {cost.gap.1017.September.multiple}. {arm:qwen3.8-flash} regresses adherence by {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.persona.holds_character.delta|abs|pts} points and increases cost to {scoreboard.qwen3.8-flash.reply_cost_usd|usd_per_1k}.

Weakest margin sits with {weakest.arm} on {weakest.criterion} at {weakest.value|pts} against threshold {weakest.threshold|pts} ({weakest.interval}), leaving a margin gap of {weakest.margin|pts}. Confounding shifts in reasoning ratio between models qualify cost attribution, and two harness drops shortened {arm:qwen3.8-flash} runs.
Run a cost-optimized variant of {arm:September} with trimmed reasoning ratios before testing alternative model architectures.

caveats.material_if: The aspect character adherence (v2) was declared post-hoc; material only if evaluated behaviors do not reflect core operational requirements.
{arm:September} was designated as control after runs completed; material only if comparison against alternative baselines was intended.
The LLM judge tier is undetermined and uncalibrated; material only if judge bias systematically distorts cross-arm adherence rankings.
